result.title: Comparative Study of Canvas- and Coordinate-Based Geometry-Conditioned Neural Networks for Real-Time Prediction of Indoor Environments with Varying Room Dimensions
result.summary: Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is computationally expensive for iterative building design. Deep learning surrogates offer faster predictions, but generalization across varying room dimensions remains challenging. This study compares two geometry-conditioned neural network surrogate models for rapid indoor airflow and temperature field prediction under varying room sizes. During the architectural design stage, this method is relevant for real-time assessment of whether conditioned supply air will effectively provide fresh and cool air throughout rooms with varying heights and lengths. The canvas-based neural network (CaNN) explicitly encodes room size by preserving different occupied regions within a fixed canvas, whereas the coordinate-based neural network (CoNN) uses normalized coordinate channels. Both employ U-Net autoencoders to separately predict airflow and temperature fields. Evaluation uses simplified rooms with varying heights and lengths as a controlled benchmark. The results show that CaNN achieves higher agreement with CFD results than CoNN, demonstrating its potential to support performance-driven building design.

AI.brief_summary: 该文比较两种几何条件化的 U-Net 代理模型（固定画布中显式编码房间尺寸的 CaNN 与使用归一化坐标通道的 CoNN）在房间尺寸变化下实时预测室内气流与温度场的效果，结果显示 CaNN 与 CFD 结果更一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心变量是几何条件的编码方式（保留绝对位置区域 vs 归一化坐标）如何影响跨尺寸泛化，可能为 LVR 中几何与位置信息怎样留在内部表示并影响泛化提供可核查线索；但该文不涉及推理状态生成、证据筛选或停止决策，仅属远端启发。
